translationRepairs: He followed Prince Zheng Jirhala on the Huguang campaign, captured Xiangtan, took Baoxing and Wugang, and sent detachments toward Yuanzhou.
He followed Prince Zheng Jirhala on the Huguang campaign, captured Xiangtan, took Baoqing and Wugang, and sent detachments toward Yuanzhou.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
The army advanced to Baoxing, where Ming general Sun Kewang had tens of thousands of men on the heights; Koerhun led a fierce assault and Kewang fled in rout.
The army advanced to Baoqing, where Ming general Sun Kewang had tens of thousands of men on the heights; Koerhun led a fierce assault and Kewang fled in rout.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
Jueshan, of the Li clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner whose family had long lived at Sarhu.
Jueshan, of the Ligiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner whose family had long lived at Sarhu.
李佳氏 is the Manchu Ligiya clan; 'Li' drops 佳 and suggests the Chinese surname Li.
He followed Prince Zheng Jirhala in campaigning in Huguang, broke Xiangtan, took Baoxing and Wugang, and divided troops to press toward Yuanzhou.
He followed Prince Zheng Jirhala in campaigning in Huguang, broke Xiangtan, took Baoqing and Wugang, and divided troops to press toward Yuanzhou.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.

The army advanced and halted at Baoxing; Ming general Sun Kewang with tens of thousands of men was encamped on the mountain crest; Koerhun directed the troops in fierce attack and Kewang fled in rout.

The army advanced and halted at Baoqing; Ming general Sun Kewang with tens of thousands of men was encamped on the mountain crest; Koerhun directed the troops in fierce attack and Kewang fled in rout.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
Jueshan, of the Li clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, whose family had long dwelt at Sarhu.
Jueshan, of the Ligiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner, whose family had long dwelt at Sarhu.
李佳氏 is the Manchu Ligiya clan; 'Li' drops 佳 and suggests the Chinese surname Li.
In the second year (1663), he followed Generals Muli Ma and Tu Hai into Huguang to suppress the Li Zicheng remnant Li Laiheng and his followers.
In the second year (1663), he followed Generals Mulima and Tuhai into Huguang to suppress the Li Zicheng remnant Li Laiheng and his followers.
穆里瑪 (Mulima) and 圖海 (Tuhai) are single Manchu personal names; splitting them into 'Muli Ma' and 'Tu Hai' makes them look like Chinese surname + given name.
In the fourteenth year (1657), he followed Grand General Luo Tuo in the descent on Guizhou.
In the fourteenth year (1657), he followed Grand General Lotu in the descent on Guizhou.
羅託 transcribes the Manchu name Lotu (a prince of the imperial clan), not a Chinese surname Luo.
Three years later he again joined a Ming campaign, captured Da'ankou, and once more routed Ming troops at Yutian.
In the third year he again joined a Ming campaign, captured Da'ankou, and once more routed Ming troops at Yutian.
三年 here is the third Tiancong year (a regnal year), not an interval of three years after Tiancong 1.
When Chief Secretary Xu Shengfang of Gongshun Wang was trapped by the enemy, Gandu plunged into the fray and brought him out.
When Chief Secretary Xu Shengfang of Prince Gongshun was trapped by the enemy, Gandu plunged into the fray and brought him out.
恭順王 is the princely title Prince Gongshun; 'Wang' is the title 'prince', not part of a name.
Gandu was a Mongol of the Bordered Blue Banner whose ancestors had moved from Yehe to Baring and taken that place as their clan name.
Gandu's ancestors had moved from Yehe to Baring and taken that place as their clan name.
The banner affiliation is stated only in s0103; s0101 says nothing about a Mongol banner.

In the fifth month of the second year the army turned to pacify Jiangnan; with gushan ejen Engetu and Malabu he secured Yixing, Kunshan, and other counties, and was promoted to third-class meiren ejen.

In the fifth month of the second year the army turned to pacify Jiangnan; with gushan ejen Engetu and Malabu he secured Yixing, Kunshan, and other counties, and was promoted to third-class meiren janggin.
梅勒章京 is the hereditary rank meiren janggin, not the banner post meiren ejen (梅勒額真).

In the fifth month of the second year, the army moved to pacify Jiangnan; again with gushan ejen Engetu, Malabu, and others he took Yixing, Kunshan, and other counties; he was advanced to third-class meiren ejen.

In the fifth month of the second year, the army moved to pacify Jiangnan; again with gushan ejen Engetu, Malabu, and others he took Yixing, Kunshan, and other counties; he was advanced to third-class meiren janggin.
梅勒章京 is the hereditary rank meiren janggin, not the banner post meiren ejen (梅勒額真).
When the army entered Fujian, Gandu outpaced the main force to take Fenshui Pass, pursued Tang Prince Zhu Yujian to Tingzhou, and received the surrender of Zhangzhou and Zhangping County.

When the army entered Fujian, Gandu outpaced the main force to take Fenshui Pass, pursued the Ming Prince of Tang, Zhu Yujian to Tingzhou, and received the surrender of Zhangzhou and Zhangping County.
明唐王聿鍵: the source names him as the Ming Prince of Tang; 'Tang Prince' drops 明 and reads as an awkward title.
He then followed Prince Yu Duoduo in the pacification of Shaanxi, capturing Tongguan and taking Xi'an.
He then followed Prince Yu Dodo in the pacification of Shaanxi, capturing Tongguan and taking Xi'an.
多鐸 is the Manchu name Dodo; 'Duoduo' is a character-by-character pinyin reading.

When Chahar fugitives scattered into Xierha and Xibitu, the khan ordered Xiteku and the Mongol Buhata tabunang to hunt them down; they killed more than seventy and seized their households and livestock.

When Chahar fugitives scattered into Xierha and Xibitu, the khan ordered Xiteku and the Mongol tabunang Buha to hunt them down; they killed more than seventy and seized their households and livestock.
蒙古布哈塔布囊: the name is 布哈 (Buha) and 塔布囊 is the title tabunang; 'Buhata tabunang' counts 塔 twice.
He again defeated Ming governor Wu Aheng, attacked Zhending, broke the eunuch Gao Qiqian's force, and pursued the fugitives to the Yuntang River.
He again defeated Ming governor Wu Aheng, attacked Zhending, broke the eunuch Gao Qiqian's force, and pursued the fugitives to the Yunliang River.
運糧河 reads Yunliang ('grain-transport') River; 糧 is liang, not tang.
For his deeds he was promoted in hereditary rank to second-class jalan commander.
For his deeds he was promoted in hereditary rank to second-class jalan janggin.
甲喇章京 is the hereditary rank jalan janggin, kept as such elsewhere in the chapter.
Again he defeated Ming governor-general Wu Aheng, attacked Zhending, broke eunuch Gao Qiqian's troops, and pursued to the Yuntang River.
Again he defeated Ming governor-general Wu Aheng, attacked Zhending, broke eunuch Gao Qiqian's troops, and pursued to the Yunliang River.
運糧河 reads Yunliang ('grain-transport') River; 糧 is liang, not tang.
For merit his hereditary rank was advanced to second-class jalan commander.
For merit his hereditary rank was advanced to second-class jalan janggin.
甲喇章京 is the hereditary rank jalan janggin, kept as such elsewhere in the chapter.
In the seventeenth year, because his kinswoman was posthumously invested as Empress Xiaohuizhang (Duanjing), he was granted first-class ashan i hafan.
In the seventeenth year, because his niece was posthumously invested as Empress Duanjing, he was granted first-class ashan i hafan.
端敬皇后 is Empress Duanjing (the Donggo consort, Eshuo's daughter); Xiaohuizhang is a different empress. 從女 is a brother's daughter, i.e. niece.
His grandfather Rubu came over with four hundred followers in Taizu's day and received the name Luksu; his son Xiha held the hereditary rank of beyi.
His grandfather Lunbu came over with four hundred followers in Taizu's day and received the name Luksu; his son Xiha held the hereditary rank of beyi.
棆布 reads Lunbu; 棆 is lun, not ru.
In the first year of Shunzhi he entered the passes with the army and was raised to third-class jalan commander in hereditary rank.
In the first year of Shunzhi he entered the passes with the army and was raised to third-class jalan janggin in hereditary rank.
甲喇章京 is the hereditary rank jalan janggin.
He was raised to second-class jalan commander in hereditary rank and appointed bayara jalan janggin.
He was raised to second-class jalan janggin in hereditary rank and appointed bayara jalan janggin.
甲喇章京 is the hereditary rank jalan janggin.
In the first year of Shunzhi, he followed in entering the passes and was advanced in hereditary rank to third-class jalan commander.
In the first year of Shunzhi, he followed in entering the passes and was advanced in hereditary rank to third-class jalan janggin.
甲喇章京 is the hereditary rank jalan janggin.
His hereditary rank was advanced to second-class jalan commander, and he was promoted to bayara jalan janggin.
His hereditary rank was advanced to second-class jalan janggin, and he was promoted to bayara jalan janggin.
甲喇章京 is the hereditary rank jalan janggin.

In the sixth year (1649) the army took Xiangtan; Yibai and gushan ejen Toto split their forces toward Hengzhou, and when more than a thousand Ming troops held a bridge and fortified a camp less than thirty li from the city, Yibai and Vice Minister Shuozhan routed them.

In the sixth year (1649) the army took Xiangtan; Yibai and gushan ejen Tong Tulai split their forces toward Hengzhou, and when more than a thousand Ming troops held a bridge and fortified a camp less than thirty li from the city, Yibai and Vice Minister Shuozhan routed them.
佟圖賴 is Tong Tulai; 'Toto' does not render these characters.
In the fifth year (1648) he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala into Hunan, where Hengzhou, Baoxing, and other prefectures were still in Ming hands.
In the fifth year (1648) he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala into Hunan, where Hengzhou, Baoqing, and other prefectures were still in Ming hands.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
Separate detachments secured Baoxing and the prefectures of Chen, Yuan, Jing, and Wugang; all were brought under control.
Separate detachments secured Baoqing and the prefectures of Chen, Yuan, Jing, and Wugang; all were brought under control.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.

In the sixth year, the army captured Xiangtan; Yibai with gushan ejen Toto and others divided troops toward Hengzhou; before reaching thirty li, more than a thousand Ming troops held a bridge and set up a camp; Yibai with Vice Minister Shuozhan attacked and routed them.

In the sixth year, the army captured Xiangtan; Yibai with gushan ejen Tong Tulai and others divided troops toward Hengzhou; before reaching thirty li, more than a thousand Ming troops held a bridge and set up a camp; Yibai with Vice Minister Shuozhan attacked and routed them.
佟圖賴 is Tong Tulai; 'Toto' does not render these characters.
In the fifth year, he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala in sweeping through Hunan; at the time Hengzhou, Baoxing, and other prefectures were still held by Ming.
In the fifth year, he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala in sweeping through Hunan; at the time Hengzhou, Baoqing, and other prefectures were still held by Ming.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
Separate armies swept Baoxing and Chen, Yuan, Jing, and Wugang prefectures; all were settled.
Separate armies swept Baoqing and Chen, Yuan, Jing, and Wugang prefectures; all were settled.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.

In the sixth year (1649) Prince Zheng Jirhala's army swept through Huguang; Ahanikan and gushan ejen Liu Zhiyuan led a separate force toward Baoxing, where Ming generals Wang Jincai and Ma Jinzhong held the city.

In the sixth year (1649) Prince Zheng Jirhala's army swept through Huguang; Ahanikan and gushan ejen Liu Zhiyuan led a separate force toward Baoqing, where Ming generals Wang Jincai and Ma Jinzhong held the city.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
The army closed on the city by night; at daybreak the Ming garrison sortied, was swiftly destroyed, and Baoxing fell.
The army closed on the city by night; at daybreak the Ming garrison sortied, was swiftly destroyed, and Baoqing fell.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.

When Ming general Wang Qiang and others attacked, Ahanikan sent acting bayara banner janggin Guerde and others to meet them; fighting on the Yuan River they won a crushing victory, killing three Ming sub-generals and more than seven hundred troops.

When Ming general Wang Qiang and others attacked, Ahanikan sent acting bayara banner janggin Du'erde and others to meet them; fighting on the Yuan River they won a crushing victory, killing three Ming sub-generals and more than seven hundred troops.
都爾德 reads Du'erde; 都 is du, not gu.
Soon he was ordered with gushan ejen Aishan and others to lead troops to Puzhou to help suppress the roving bandits.
Soon he was ordered with gushan ejen Ashan and others to lead troops to Puzhou to help suppress the roving bandits.
The Songshan garrison commander launched a night raid on the Qing camp, and infantry also attacked the Bordered Yellow Banner Mongol outposts; Ahanikan drove both back.
The Songshan garrison commander launched a night raid on the Qing camp, and infantry also attacked the Plain Yellow Banner Mongol outposts; Ahanikan drove both back.
正黃旗 is the Plain Yellow Banner; 鑲黃 would be Bordered Yellow.

In the sixth year, Prince Zheng Jirhala's army swept Huguang; Ahanikan with gushan ejen Liu Zhiyuan as a separate commander led troops toward Baoxing; Ming generals Wang Jincai and Ma Jinzhong held the city.

In the sixth year, Prince Zheng Jirhala's army swept Huguang; Ahanikan with gushan ejen Liu Zhiyuan as a separate commander led troops toward Baoqing; Ming generals Wang Jincai and Ma Jinzhong held the city.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.
The army at night pressed close to the city; at daybreak Ming troops sortied to fight; he urgently attacked and annihilated them, then captured Baoxing.
The army at night pressed close to the city; at daybreak Ming troops sortied to fight; he urgently attacked and annihilated them, then captured Baoqing.
寶慶 reads Baoqing; 慶 is qing, not xing.

Ming general Wang Qiang and others came to attack; Ahanikan dispatched acting bayara banner janggin Guerde and others to meet the attack; they fought on the Yuan River and inflicted a great defeat, beheading three assistant generals and more than seven hundred soldiers.

Ming general Wang Qiang and others came to attack; Ahanikan dispatched acting bayara banner janggin Du'erde and others to meet the attack; they fought on the Yuan River and inflicted a great defeat, beheading three assistant generals and more than seven hundred soldiers.
都爾德 reads Du'erde; 都 is du, not gu.
Soon he was ordered together with gushan ejen Aishan and others to lead troops to Puzhou to assist in suppressing roving bandits.
Soon he was ordered together with gushan ejen Ashan and others to lead troops to Puzhou to assist in suppressing roving bandits.
The Songshan garrison commander made a night raid on our army; again he sent infantry to violate the Bordered Yellow Banner Mongol outpost area; Ahanikan struck and drove them back.
The Songshan garrison commander made a night raid on our army; again he sent infantry to violate the Plain Yellow Banner Mongol outpost area; Ahanikan struck and drove them back.
正黃旗 is the Plain Yellow Banner; 鑲黃 would be Bordered Yellow.
The army swept through Hongjiang, broke Yuan Zongdi's tenth camp, and captured Yuanzhou.
The army swept through Hongjiang, broke Yuan Zongdi's ten camps, and captured Yuanzhou.
袁宗第十營 is Yuan Zongdi's ten camps (十營), not a 'tenth' camp.
When the Shunzhi emperor planned to move the capital to Yanjing, he ordered inner minister Helo to hold Shengjing; Ahanikan and meile ejen Shuozhan commanded the left and right wings as his deputies.

When the Shunzhi emperor planned to move the capital to Yanjing, he ordered inner minister Holohui to hold Shengjing; Ahanikan and meile ejen Shuozhan commanded the left and right wings as his deputies.
何洛會 is the Manchu name Holohui; 'Helo' drops 會.
When Bumbogor led six thousand Uriankhai troops in a surprise attack on the Plain Blue Banner rear guard, Suohai laid an ambush—and Ahanikan fought in it.
When Bumbogor led six thousand troops of the two Ula in a surprise attack on the Plain Blue Banner rear guard, Suohai laid an ambush—and Ahanikan fought in it.
兩烏喇兵 are troops of the two Ula; nothing in the source names the Uriankhai.

In the third year he followed Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong, campaigned through Shaanxi, and with Minister Xingne defeated generals including Gao Rushi before pushing into Sichuan, where he repeatedly routed Xianzhong's forces.

In the third year he followed Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong, campaigned through Shaanxi, and with Minister Xingne defeated generals including Gao Ruli before pushing into Sichuan, where he repeatedly routed Xianzhong's forces.
高汝礪 reads Gao Ruli; 礪 is li, not shi.

In the third year, he followed Prince Su Haoge in suppressing Zhang Xianzhong, raided Shaanxi, with Minister Xingne struck Xianzhong's generals Gao Rushi and others, then descended into Sichuan and repeatedly defeated Xianzhong's troops.
